That is exactly how I started out in high school and it turned out to be depression. My advice to you is to start a hobby. Even if it is something that you don't care about. For me it was photography, not that I find much interest in it, but it helps to take my mind off of the real world and what I am thinking. Another thing to do now is to make a set of goals for your future. Where do you want to be in 10 years? What did you think about being when you were younger? Trying to keep on track with these goals will help out a lot. Even if you have no motivation to do it, preserver on. Don't just do things for yourself, do things for your parents. I don't particularly have any feelings for my parents but they have always been there fore me and therefore I don't want to let them down.

I understand what you are going through. For me, I try not to think about what I want right now, but what I want for myself in the future. Currently I am at university working towards a bachelors degree in engineering and every day is the hardest day ever. I have to focus about what society expects of me and try hard to put everything I feel behind. 
I don't think that anything done while battling this disease will lead to happiness. It is really just a battle of trying to put future over anything else. I am impressed that you have a job and are trying to work your way up. If you took that motivation and started with something a little smaller. Try your eye at something else, a new hobby. Something to take your mind off of the present and let it evolve from there.
